chunks: It is not permissible for the sacrificial animals from camels except the thani — that which has completed five years and entered its sixth. For cattle and goats, the thani suffices — that which has completed one year and entered its second. From sheep, the jadha' (around one year) suffices.
An animal with a defect/blemish does not suffice as a sacrifice.

A cow suffices for five persons if they are from one household; a bull for one; a badana (camel) for seven; a jazur (slaughter camel) for ten from different households; and a ram suffices for a man and his household.
When sacrificial animals are scarce, a single sheep suffices for seventy persons.
The sacrificial animal is to be divided into three thirds: one third is eaten, one third is gifted, and one third is given in charity.

key_terms.الأضاحي: Udhiya — sacrificial animals slaughtered at Eid al-Adha
key_terms.البدنة: Badana — a camel designated for sacrifice, valid for seven people
key_terms.الثني: Thani — an animal that has completed a specific age threshold and entered the next year; for camels, five years; for cattle/goats, one year
key_terms.الجذع: Jadha' — a young sheep that has reached approximately eight months to a year; accepted by Shia jurisprudence as sufficient for sacrifice
key_terms.الجزور: Jazur — a slaughter camel, valid for ten people from different households
key_terms.عوار: Blemish/defect — a physical impairment that disqualifies an animal from being a valid sacrificial offering

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the sacrificial animal (udhiya) in Shia Islam regarding age, type, and division of meat?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the detailed jurisprudential rules for the udhiya (sacrificial animal at Eid al-Adha) as transmitted in al-Amali of Sheikh Saduq. It specifies the minimum age requirements for different species — five years for camels, one year for cattle and goats, and approximately one year (jadha') for sheep — and prohibits animals with defects. It also details how many people each type of animal can represent, and introduces a dispensation for scarcity, and mandates the three-way division of the meat (personal consumption, gifting, and charity).
word_analysis: and it is to be divided

en.bilal-muhammad: It is not permissible to sacrifice except a grown camel – that which has completed five years and has entered its sixth. It is permissible to sacrifice a grown cow and goat that has completed one year and entered its second. It is permissible to sacrifice a lamb that has reached eight or nine months to a year.
It is not permissible to sacrifice an animal with blemishes.
A cow can suffice for five individuals if they are members of a family; a bull for one, and a camel for seven …
A sacrifice is split into thirds: one third for eating, one third for gifting, and one third for charity.
